items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: the big bands of the ‘30s, Henry Hall, Ambrose Roy Fox, Jack Hilton and so on, had some very good bands

ctx.x: Well I think it’s unusual. I mean my father said, “She’s jazz crazy you know.” And I can remember going to someone’s home and she’d bought some records, she had a brother in the RAF or something like that, and invited me to go around, and I sort of, I remember going into the house, and the girl’s father was sitting there having his tea, which is like dinner for us, for the working man. And he was sitting there sort of digging into his tea and this girl put on the record, the phonograph you know, wound it up. And…

doing this kind of thing. I mean and this man’s looking at me like I had descended from another planet. I mean again, they didn’t understand. Because jazz music was really a very esoteric type of sound. We’ve had good bands incidentally in England. I mean don’t forget that Coleman Hawkins and the Ramblers, the Dutch Ramblers and stuff, the big bands of the ‘30s, Henry Hall, Ambrose Roy Fox, Jack Hilton and so on, had some very good bands, and they had good support from the American musicians that chose to come…
Do you recall what kind of music your parents listened to?
